### Diagnosis

The current bug report indicates that the method `SimplexSolver.optimize(...)` is giving bad results with commons-math3-3.0 in a simple test problem, although it worked well in commons-math-2.2.

By looking at the failing test `testMath781`, it constructs a `LinearObjectiveFunction` with coefficients `{2, 6, 7}` and a constant term of `0`. It then creates a list of `LinearConstraint`s and sets up a `SimplexSolver` to optimize the objective function with the constraints. The test asserts that the first element of the solution point is greater than `0`.

Inspecting the `LinearObjectiveFunction` constructor reveals that it initializes a new `ArrayRealVector` with the given coefficients and constant term. This initialization might be different in commons-math3-3.0 compared to commons-math-2.2, potentially leading to the discrepancy in results.

However, without the code implementation of the `SimplexSolver.optimize` method, it is challenging to pinpoint the exact root cause of the bad results. It is recommended to review the implementation of the `SimplexSolver.optimize` method in commons-math3-3.0 to identify any changes that might affect the optimization process.

### Suggested Fix
- `org.apache.commons.math3.optimization.linear.SimplexSolver.optimize(org.apache.commons.math3.optimization.linear.LinearObjectiveFunction,java.util.Collection,org.apache.commons.math3.optimization.GoalType,boolean)`

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
